LESSON: VOLUME AND CAPACITY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurements
Topic 3.4: Volume and Capacity
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Volume and Capacity, part of Measurements in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How do we use volume and capacity in daily activities? 2. Why do we measure volume?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. make a cube of sides 1 metre using locally available materials in purposive groups/pairs or as individuals. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional part of the body or be assisted by their peers to carry out the activity.

2. Discuss in purposive groups/pairs or as individuals and work out the conversions of cm cube (cm3 ) to m cube (m3 ) and vice versa. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they carry out the activity.

3. Collect labeled containers of different volume and capacity from the environment. Learners 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. make a cube of sides 1 metre using locally available materials in purposive groups/pairs or as individuals. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional part of the body or be assisted by their peers to carry out the activity.
2. Discuss in purposive groups/pairs or as individuals and work out the conversions of cm cube (cm3 ) to m cube (m3 ) and vice versa. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they carry out the activity.
3. Collect labeled containers of different volume and capacity from the environment. Learners 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Volume and Capacity together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and problem solving: as the learner creates a conversion table of units of volume.

● Creativity and Imagination: as the learner creates models of cubes and cuboids.

Values

● Responsibility: as the learner works with peers and share different tasks in making models.

● Peace: as the learner discusses and makes models for different volumes and capacities.
